label: gate1_v5
why: Lines 1-3 work. 'You are the horse head' is a fresh angle, and the [6910万] tag catches my eye. 'Bought it and then gave it away' (#3 [捐了出去]) is a small puzzle I want answered: why spend 69 million and give it away? I'd stay for at least the next 10 seconds. I'm not hooked for sure, though. I already half-know this story (何鸿燊, 马首, 圆明园 comes up every year in news and textbooks), so the hook has to quickly give me something I don't already know.
first_moment_I_got_curious: #11-#13 (~0:32-0:40). '每两小时，轮到谁，谁就喷水 / 你，是午时 / 正午12点，十二个[一起喷水]'. I didn't know the twelve heads worked as a water clock. This is the first thing that's new to me, and it gives 'you' a job, a personality. The money hook in #2-#3 got my attention, but this is where I actually got curious.
where_I_would_swipe_away: #4-#9 (~0:10-0:28): #4-#7 squeeze the whole story into four dates (1860 抢走 / 伦敦 买走 / 2007 锤子没有落下 / 2020 回家). Then #9 jumps back to 乾隆 and starts over. My brain goes 'ok, I just got the summary, now it's rewinding to the beginning.' This is my biggest swipe risk. If #11 weren't so close, I might be gone here. '2007年，锤子没有落下' also means nothing to me yet at #6.
#18 (~0:54): '一百多年后，你出现在伦敦' repeats #5 ('在伦敦，被人买走'). It feels like I'm hearing the same line twice. Small dip.

#21-#23 (~1:03-1:12): '2000年 牛猴虎上拍 / 三个都被买了回来 / 2003年 何鸿燊买回了猪首'. This is the dates-and-animals list stretch. It isn't about 'me' (the horse) anymore, it's a roll call of siblings. I'd scroll here if I was tired.

#48-#51 (~2:29-2:42): after the emotional #46-#47 ending, it goes back to counting (六个/五个) and then adds a 'maybe-dragon, can't tell if it's real' detour. That makes the ending muddy. I'd likely swipe before #52, so I'd miss the question meant to get me commenting.
lines_I_did_not_understand: #6 '2007年，锤子没有落下': at this point I don't know what hammer or why it matters. It only makes sense at #25. It's a teaser, but it reads like a riddle I can't solve.
#19 '[几十万美元]': this is vague. I need a number to compare with #29's '贵了二十多倍', and 'tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands' is too fuzzy for 20x to land.
#22 '三个都被买了回来': bought back by whom? The video names 何鸿燊 in the next line, so I assumed it was him too, which is probably wrong.
#32-#33 '买家却拒绝付款 / 他认为：这本就是中国的': who is 他? An anonymous buyer refused to pay? I'm confused about whether this was a Chinese patriot or something else. It's the coolest moment, and he has no name.
#34 '2013年，鼠和兔被无偿送回': sent back by whom? The line right before was the refusing buyer, so I'd assume he sent them back, which makes no sense (he never got them). Missing the giver's identity.
#26 '国家文物局反对公开拍卖' then #27 '私下买下了你': so did the government stop the auction, or did 何鸿燊? The cause and effect isn't clear.
#43 '园里唯一幸存的古建筑': which building? A name would make this a fact I could repeat to a friend.
#45 '研究的人说：你这一路被撞过': 'researchers said' is vague. It's still a nice detail.

Number overload: twelve, 11 brothers, 3, 1, 2, seven back in China, only you at 圆明园, 11 still missing, 6 in museums, 5 not in China. #8 says '五个没回来' and #47 says '还差[十一个]'. For a second I thought the video contradicted itself, until #48-#49 explained it.
dates_list_feel: Yes, in two places. (1) #4-#7: four dates in four lines with no context. (2) #21-#36: 2000, 2003, 2007, 2009, 2013, 2019, 2020 in quick succession. The 2007 part (#24-#29) and the 2009 refusing-to-pay part (#30-#33) have real drama. 2000/2003/2013 are just bookkeeping. I counted 13 year mentions in a 2:45 video.
takeaway_in_my_words: The horse head was one of twelve fountain heads that took turns spouting water like a clock. It got looted in 1860, sold around for 100+ years, and 何鸿燊 bought it privately for 69 million HKD and gave it to the country. He died a few months before it actually went back to 圆明园 in 2020. It's the only one of the twelve that is back in the garden itself, and five are still abroad.
surprise_that_stuck: Two things. First, #36-#37: 何鸿燊 died in May 2020 and the horse went home in December 2020, so he never saw it. That hit me. Second, #42: of the seven back in China, only the horse is actually in 圆明园. I always assumed the returned ones went back there. The water-clock detail (#11-#13) plus its callback at #46-#47 ('本该一起喷水，现在还差十一个') is the best-built moment of the video.
title_I_would_click: 3) 6910万买下，又捐了出去. Money + 'why would anyone do that' is exactly what makes me stop scrolling. It's a question I want answered, and it doesn't sound like a news headline. 2) 假如你是圆明园马首 is my second choice: the second-person angle is different, but it reads a bit like a 营销号 template ('假如你是…'), and I'd guess it's an AI-narrated history clip. 1) 马首回家，用了160年 sounds like a CCTV/人民日报 caption. Correct and touching, but I feel like I've already seen it, so I'd scroll past.
title_that_misleads: 3) slightly. It promises a story about the buyer, but he's a side character until #27, and most of the video is the horse's journey and its siblings' auctions. Also, '6910万' with no currency reads as RMB; the video says 港元 only at #28. Not a big lie, just a small bait-and-switch in focus. 1) and 2) are accurate.
what_I_would_comment: "不该花钱买！花钱买就是认了抢劫是合法的，那个拒绝付款的大哥才是真的牛" (a reply to #52). Or, if I didn't make it to #52: "何鸿燊没等到那天，破防了".

for_frames_only.what_this_says_in_5s: No frames were provided for this gate. I only read the subtitle lines and the titles.

suggestions_as_a_viewer_not_editor: Make #4-#7 one or two lines, or cut them. The restart at #9 is where I'd leave.
Give #19 a real number so the '二十多倍' payoff at #29 lands.
Say who refused to pay (#32) and who sent the rat and rabbit back (#34). Those are the best surprises, and right now they're anonymous.
Cut or shorten #50-#51 (the possible dragon head). Going straight from #49 to #52 keeps the ending clean.
